$comment: LICENSE-PENDING — see docs/non_ratified/LICENSE_PENDING.md. DocumentBuffer per FB-RAT-WS-001/003/004/005. FB-RAT-WS-003 (crash-safe buffers: dirty buffers survive Activity recreation/process death/reboot until explicit save or discard) is why `dirty`+`journalSequence` are both present — journalSequence is what a RecoverySnapshot/WorkspaceJournal.restore() uses to reconstitute exactly this buffer's un-persisted edits. `state` follows the DocumentBufferState machine in WORKSPACE_KERNEL_SPEC.md §4 (CLOSED -> OPEN_CLEAN -> OPEN_DIRTY -> SAVING -> OPEN_CLEAN | SAVE_FAILED; OPEN_DIRTY -> CONFLICTED -> MERGING -> OPEN_DIRTY). The `dirty` and `conflictState` fields are each pinned to `state` via `allOf`/`if`/`then` below so a wire payload cannot claim an internally-contradictory buffer (e.g. state=OPEN_CLEAN with dirty=true, or state=CONFLICTED with conflictState=null) — see fixtures/workspace/invalid/document-buffer-dirty-state-contradiction.invalid.json and fixtures/workspace/invalid/document-buffer-conflict-state-mismatch.invalid.json.
title: DocumentBuffer

bufferId.description: Globally unique stable ID for this buffer (FB-RAT-COM-002), independent of `resourceUri` — a buffer keeps its identity across a save-as/rename in the same editing session if the implementation chooses to model it that way.

dirty.description: Whether this buffer's in-memory content differs from its last known persisted content (FB-RAT-WS-003). Structurally pinned to `state` below: false only for CLOSED/OPEN_CLEAN, true for every other state.

baseRevision.description: The provider revision this buffer's content was opened/last-synced from, used as `expectedRevision` for an optimistic-concurrency write (FB-RAT-WS-004). Null for a buffer with no remote counterpart yet (e.g. a new unsaved file).

contentRevision.description: Opaque revision/hash of this buffer's CURRENT in-memory content, advanced on every edit. Distinct from `baseRevision` (which never changes until a successful save rebases it).

encoding.description: Text encoding of this buffer's content, e.g. 'UTF-8', 'UTF-16LE'.

lineEndings.description: Line-ending convention detected/in-use for this buffer. MIXED means the buffer contains more than one convention (FB-RAT-COM-009 relevance: a save that silently normalizes MIXED endings without telling the user is a legibility violation, not just a formatting nicety).

journalSequence.description: The highest `BufferJournalEntry.sequence` applied to this buffer so far (FB-RAT-COM-004 — monotonic sequence). Used by WorkspaceJournal.restore() to know exactly which journal entries still need replaying for this buffer after a crash.

remoteRevision.description: The provider revision that was found to differ from `baseRevision` at write/refresh time, triggering the conflict (FB-RAT-WS-004).

remoteSummary.description: Optional plain-language summary of what changed remotely, for accessibility (FB-RAT-COM-009) — MUST NOT rely on a diff-only visual to convey that a conflict exists.

conflictState.description: Non-null only while `state` is CONFLICTED or MERGING; null otherwise (structurally enforced below).

lastSaveError.description: Non-null only while `state` is SAVE_FAILED; null otherwise (structurally enforced below). Carries why the last save attempt failed (FB-RAT-COM-007), so a SAVE_FAILED buffer is not just a bare status flag with no explanation — `userMessage` gives this state its accessibility-required textual semantics (FB-RAT-COM-009).

unknownFields.description: Bag for fields a decoder received but did not recognize, preserved for round-trip (FB-RAT-COM-003).

ErrorEnvelope.description: Mirrors schemas/common/error.schema.json's ErrorEnvelope — duplicated locally rather than cross-file $ref'd, same standalone-file tradeoff COMMON_CONVENTIONS.md documents for IntegrityRef.
